newsitem.title: CHINA: China declares war on feudal, foreign names.
newsitem.headline: China declares war on feudal, foreign names.

text.p: Chinese government officials, caught in a backlash against Western cultural imperialism, have declared a ban on names deemed too foreign or feudal.

"Names displaying unhealthy content and cultural colonialism would no longer be used in China because they harm the national interest and dignity," the China Daily on Thursday quoted Vice-Minister of Civil Affairs Li Baoku as saying.
Many developers and businessmen gave places "unhealthy" names to seek profits and due to a desire to appear more Western or fashionable, Li said.

"Many of China's streets, districts, public buildings and leisure facilities are using names that are vulgar, obscure or insulting to national dignity," the newspaper quoted a circular issued by the ministry as saying.
The newspaper cited an entertainment centre in Wuhan in the central province of Hubei named Formosa -- the name given to the island of Taiwan by Portuguese sailors in the 17th century.
Beijing has considered Taiwan a rebel province since the two were separated at the end of a civil war in 1949.
Other taboo monikers would be those with a feudal ring such as "Imperial Mansions", it said.
Local officials should force improper names to be changed and the ministry would soon issue a set of regulations detailing the registration and approval of names of public places, it said.
"The problem has aroused strong public concern and could have an adverse effect on the social values of children," it quoted one urban survey as saying.
